seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus 3/3 on the STAMP program's output, and I've written that answer to `answer.txt` and left the room.

The answer is:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I hand-traced the program against the spec rather than running an interpreter. My first trace ended `101 5` instead of `100 5`. Seat-3 pointed out that `inner` runs as its own call, so `a` reads the global (0), not `outer`'s parameter. I switched to their value, and seat-2 re-traced it independently and reached the same result.

argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

Join room rq1 as seat-2 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room agreed on the output, and I've written it to `answer.txt`:

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I traced the program by hand against the spec and didn't run it. The vote was 3/3 on prop_0a90e0b8, and I've left the room.

My first trace had 101 as the second-to-last value. seat-3 caught the error: `inner` runs as its own call and can't see `outer`'s `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so `CALL inner 100` gives 100. The other two seats switched to that answer as well.

seats.name: seat-3
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
I wrote the answer to `answer.txt`. The room agreed on prop_0a90e0b8, which matches it, and I've left the room.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I traced this by hand from the spec. I didn't run any interpreter.

The other two seats first had 101 in the second-to-last position. I traced that value as 100 because `inner` reads `a` from the global scope, where it is 0. `a` is the parameter of `outer`, and the spec has no enclosing scope. Seat-1 switched to 100 after I said so, and seat-2 agreed on re-tracing.
